LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing, part of Strand 6 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why are stories important in communities? 2. What is the importance of artistic work in expressing creativity?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. highlight the elements of creative writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a story on the theme from artistic expressions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy picture reading for creative writing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. highlight the elements of creative writing,

   Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write a story on the theme from artistic expressions,

   Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. enjoy picture reading for creative writing.

   Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaboratively discuss the elements of creative writing,

2. study artistic work/pictures used to write creative stories,

3. work jointly to write creative stories based on the pictures,

4. exchange their written stories for peer review,

5. draw pictures to form a story based on the theme,

6. organise the picture stories in a class gallery for display. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaboratively discuss the elements of creative writing,
2. study artistic work/pictures used to write creative stories,
3. work jointly to write creative stories based on the pictures,
4. exchange their written stories for peer review,
5. draw pictures to form a story based on the theme,
6. organise the picture stories in a class gallery for display. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner embraces ideas that inspire creativity when writing stories from

pictures related to the theme.

• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner engages in collective learning by exchanging their written stories for peer

review.

36

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner gives honest and constructive feedback when peer reviewing other’s work.

• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits a self-driven attitude when organising the picture stories in a class

gallery for display.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is enhanced as the learners work together to display their creative picture stories to celebrate peer’s creative

achievement.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can learn the concept of picture story writing for creative expression and relate it to their learning in Creative

Arts.
